name: Azmaveth
overview: Azmaveth is a male figure mentioned in the post-exilic period, noted primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his connection to the restoration community is significant. The location Beth-azmaveth is also referenced, linking his name geographically in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Azmaveth means 'strong one of death' and is also associated with 'camel fodder' or a 'plant of the plumose family.' This proper name, found in Ezra 2:21, was not given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azmaveth as a descendant of Jacob, indicating his place within the broader Israelite lineage. Beyond this, his family is noted through his sons or descendants who participated in the return to Judah, but no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Azmaveth's importance lies in his role as an ancestor whose lineage was part of the post-exilic restoration of Judah, emphasizing continuity of the Israelite people after captivity. The mention of Beth-azmaveth further anchors his name within the biblical geography, underscoring the historical and communal context of the returnees. His presence in Ezra highlights the faithfulness of God's people in returning to their homeland and reestablishing their covenant community.
